title: Introducing yourself
summary: Say who you are with the topic particle は and the polite copula です.

drill.prompt: Which particle marks the topic of a sentence?
drill.explain: は marks the topic — spelled は, pronounced "wa".

drill.prompt: です attaches to which of these?
drill.explain: です follows nouns and な-adjectives; verbs use the ます form instead.

title: It is / it is not
summary: Link nouns with の and make negative statements with じゃありません.

drill.prompt: How do you say "my book" — where does の go?
drill.explain: The possessor comes first: わたし の 本.

drill.prompt: The polite negative copula is…
drill.explain: じゃありません (or ではありません) replaces です entirely.

title: Casual statements & simple questions
summary: Meet the plain copula だ and turn statements into questions with か.

drill.prompt: What do you add to the end of a statement to make it a question?
drill.explain: か at the end turns a statement into a question; word order stays the same.

drill.prompt: だ is the … form of the copula.
drill.explain: だ is the plain copula; です is its polite counterpart.

title: Subjects & question words
summary: Use が for the subject and the core question words なに・だれ・どこ.

drill.prompt: Which particle usually marks the subject of a question word (e.g. "who")?
drill.explain: Question-word subjects take が: だれが…, not だれは.

drill.prompt: "Where" is…
drill.explain: どこ = where; だれ = who; なに = what; いつ = when.

title: Doing things (polite)
summary: Mark the object with を and use the polite ます form.

drill.prompt: Which particle marks the direct object of a transitive verb?
drill.explain: を marks the direct object; it is written を but pronounced "o".

drill.prompt: The polite form of のむ is…
drill.explain: う-verb のむ → stem のみ + ます = のみます.

title: Where and how
summary: に for destinations and times, で for the place of an action and the means.

drill.prompt: "I study at school." Which particle marks 学校 (the place of the action)?
drill.explain: で marks where an action happens; に marks existence or destination.

drill.prompt: Which particle marks the means of transport ("by train")?
drill.explain: 電車で = by train — で marks the means.

title: Going places, doing things with people
summary: へ for direction, と for "and" between nouns and "with" a person.

drill.prompt: The particle へ (direction) is pronounced…
drill.explain: へ is written "he" but pronounced "e" as a particle.

drill.prompt: To list "coffee and tea" exhaustively, use…
drill.explain: と joins a complete list of nouns (for a partial list, use や).

title: Also, and there is
summary: も for "also", and ある for things that exist.

drill.prompt: も replaces which particles?
drill.explain: も means "also" and replaces は, が or を (never stacks with them).

drill.prompt: Which verb of existence is used for inanimate things?
drill.explain: ある is for inanimate things; いる is for living things.

title: There is (living things) & dictionary form
summary: いる for people and animals, and the verb groups behind the dictionary form.

drill.prompt: Which verb of existence is used for people and animals?
drill.explain: いる is for animate beings; ある is for inanimate things.

drill.prompt: Which of these is an う-verb despite ending in る?
drill.explain: 帰る is an う-verb (帰ります). The others are る-verbs.

title: Describing things
summary: い-adjectives that conjugate themselves and な-adjectives that need な.

drill.prompt: How do you connect a な-adjective to a following noun ("a quiet room")?
drill.explain: な-adjectives take な before a noun: 静かな部屋.

drill.prompt: い-adjectives before a noun take…
drill.explain: い-adjectives attach directly: 大きい車 (no particle).

title: Not, and was
summary: Negate and past-tense adjectives: 〜くない / 〜じゃない and 〜かった / でした.

drill.prompt: The negative of the い-adjective たかい is…
drill.explain: Drop い, add くない: たか + くない.

drill.prompt: The past of the い-adjective たかい is…
drill.explain: Drop い, add かった: たかかった (polite: たかかったです).

title: Saying no (verbs)
summary: Polite ません and the plain ない form.

drill.prompt: The polite past negative of a verb is…
drill.explain: Polite past negative = 〜ませんでした.

drill.prompt: The plain negative of かう is…
drill.explain: う-verbs shift う → わ before ない: かう → かわない.

title: The て form & requests
summary: Build the て form and make polite requests with 〜てください.

drill.prompt: The て form of かく is…
drill.explain: く → いて: かく → かいて (いく is the exception → いって).

drill.prompt: "Please don't do (it)" uses…
drill.explain: Negative request = ない form + でください.

title: Linking actions & the plain past
summary: Chain actions with the て form and meet the plain past た form.

drill.prompt: When chaining clauses with the て form, which clause carries the tense?
drill.explain: Only the final verb marks tense; earlier clauses use the て form.

drill.prompt: The plain past of のむ is…
drill.explain: む/ぶ/ぬ verbs → んだ: のむ → のんだ.

title: Wanting
summary: Want to do (〜たい) and want to have (〜がほしい).

drill.prompt: 〜たい attaches to…
drill.explain: 〜たい attaches to the ます-stem: たべ + たい = たべたい.

drill.prompt: With ほしい, the wanted thing is marked with…
drill.explain: 〜がほしい: the desired thing takes が.

title: Can do, let's do
summary: Ability with 〜ことができる and suggestions with 〜ましょう.

drill.prompt: 〜ことができる follows which verb form?
drill.explain: Dictionary form + ことができる: 話すことができる.

drill.prompt: "Let's go" is…
drill.explain: 〜ましょう proposes a shared action: いきましょう.

title: Inviting & giving reasons
summary: Polite invitations with 〜ませんか and reasons with から.

drill.prompt: 〜ませんか is used to…
drill.explain: 〜ませんか is a soft invitation ("won't you…?").

drill.prompt: から meaning "because" comes…
drill.explain: Reason + から + result: the reason comes first.

title: Softer reasons & contrast
summary: ので for softer reasons and が for "but".

drill.prompt: After a noun, ので links with…
drill.explain: Noun/な-adjective + な + ので: 学生なので.

drill.prompt: As a conjunction, が means…
drill.explain: Clause + が + clause expresses a mild contrast ("but").

title: Comparing
summary: Comparatives with より / のほうが and superlatives with いちばん.

drill.prompt: In a comparison, より marks…
drill.explain: より marks the thing compared against; のほうが marks the one with more.

drill.prompt: The group in a superlative (いちばん) is marked with…
drill.explain: Superlatives use で or の中で for the group.

title: Time & frequency
summary: Spans with 〜から〜まで, approximation with ごろ/ぐらい, and frequency adverbs.

drill.prompt: "From 9 to 5" uses…
drill.explain: から marks the start, まで the end: 9時から5時まで.

drill.prompt: For "about 3 o'clock" (a point in time) use…
drill.explain: ごろ = around a point in time; ぐらい = about an amount/duration.

drill.prompt: Which adverbs require a negative verb?
drill.explain: あまり and ぜんぜん pair with a negative verb (not much / not at all).
